title: Several actions on a replica: a call or an email, judged against every row's true lift
request: Phase 10 'What remains' item 7: 34.2's choice of several actions was tested on random tables only; a two-action replica.
spec: dclab_core/replicas/retention_actions.py (customers at risk of leaving; a random test of no contact, an email, a call; a customer kept is worth a year of fees; a call costs 15 and is few, an email 0.5; the true lift of each action per row in facts) and tests/test_retention_actions.py (each action's lift from an uplift learner on the training rows, value = lift x worth - cost, choose_actions under the call capacity, judged on the true lifts against emailing everyone, calling only, a random assignment of the same counts and the best possible).
plan: A replica with two actions whose helped customers differ, its traps written for the knowledge base
Estimate each action's lift per row from the arms on training rows only
Assign with choose_actions under the call capacity
Judge on the true lifts against single-action and random policies and the best possible
Write the test as measured, not as hoped

decisions.decision: Each action's lift from its own arm against no contact (a learner per action)
decisions.why: only the random test's arms tell an action's effect; comparing contacted rows with the rest would mix the arms
measured on five seeds: above the T-learner on every one (for example 15.28 against 13.85 a customer on seed 0)

decisions.decision: The test asserts what was measured: beats calling only and random on every seed, emailing everyone on at least 4 of 5
decisions.why: on seed 2 both learners fall short of emailing everyone; writing every seed as a win would hide a real limit

change: dclab_core/replicas/retention_actions.py; tests/test_retention_actions.py (2 tests); evidence/business_examples rebuilt (the replica's traps as an example); docs/guides/PHASE10_ABILITIES_PLAN.md item 7

findings.defect: the two-action assignment can lose to emailing everyone
findings.scenario: seed 2: 12.43 a customer (X-learner) and 11.97 (T-learner) against 12.65 for emailing everyone; the true best is 17.06
findings.cause: an email lifts most customers by about half a point; times a year of fees less 0.5 it is a small positive value, and estimation noise turns many of them negative, so those customers get nothing
findings.fix: not changed: recorded as open (act on a cheap action unless its estimated value is clearly negative, with an interval per row's value)

findings.scenario: replacing uplift.TLearner with XLearner to compare them: XLearner.fit calls TLearner, now itself, until RecursionError
findings.cause: patching a name the replacement uses
findings.fix: the learner is a parameter of the test's run function

measurements.name: two actions on retention_actions, seeds 0 to 4, X-learner
measurements.gate: the assignment beats calling only and a random assignment of the same counts on every seed, emailing everyone on at least 4 of 5, within 30% of the best possible
measurements.result: value a customer chosen / best / email everyone / calls only / random: seed 0 15.28/17.07/12.74/3.84/9.67; seed 1 15.05/17.08/12.65/4.62/10.25; seed 2 12.43/17.06/12.65/1.52/8.81; seed 3 15.06/17.34/12.92/4.34/10.14; seed 4 14.56/17.33/12.85/2.47/9.88; calls kept to capacity on every seed
limits: the bar was set after this one measurement: the test guards against regression, it is not a pre-registered gate
one invented replica, randomised arms only

outcome: Several actions are now judged on a replica with known lifts: the assignment beats single-action and random policies, and the cheap action's small lift is the open weakness.
lessons: A cheap action that helps a little is lost to estimation noise first: judge it against 'do it for everyone', not only against doing nothing
Write a test as the measurement came out, and record the miss as an open item
risks: The X-learner's better seeds may not hold on observational data (no random arms)
